description: Notice Type: Sources Sought Notice ID: N4008026RAEIDIQINDUSTRIAL Date: Tuesday, July 21, 2026 Response Date: Monday, August 24, 2026, 2:00 PM EST NAICS: 541330-Engineering Services This is a Sources Sought Notice. This notice does not constitute a request for proposal, request for quote, or invitation for bid. The intent of this notice is to identify potential offerors for market research purposes and determine whether to set aside this requirement for small business concerns, including firms certified by the U.S. Small Business Administration (SBA) as 8(a), HUBZone, Service-Disabled Veteran-Owned Small Business (SDVOSB), Women-Owned Small Business (WOSB), or Economically Disadvantaged Women-Owned Small Business (EDWOSB), with the qualifications, experience, personnel, and capability to perform multidisciplinary architect-engineering (A/E) services in support of projects at military installations within the Naval Facilities Engineering Systems Command (NAVFAC) Washington Area of Responsibility (AOR), including Washington, DC, Maryland, and Virginia (DMV). TELEPHONIC SUBMISSIONS AND QUESTIONS WILL NOT BE ACCEPTED OR ACKNOWLEDGED AS THIS IS A SOURCES SOUGHT NOTICE ONLY. In accordance with FAR 15.201(e), responses to this notice are not offers and cannot be accepted by the Government to form a binding contract. The Government will not pay or reimburse respondents for any costs, administrative expenses, or effort associated with preparing or submitting information in response to this announcement or any subsequent follow-up requests. All costs associated with responding will be solely at the interested party's expense. No basis for a claim against the Government shall arise from responding to this Sources Sought Notice. NAVFAC Washington anticipates awarding two stand-alone Indefinite Delivery/Indefinite Quantity (IDIQ) Architect-Engineering (A/E) contracts: the "Blue" NAVFAC Washington Regional A/E IDIQ and the "Gold" NAVFAC Washington Regional A/E IDIQ. The anticipated maximum value of each contract is $249,000,000. Each contract is expected to include a two-year base period, a three-year option period, and a six-month extension option. NAVFAC Washington seeks qualified firms with relevant experience, personnel, and capabilities to provide multidisciplinary A/E services for projects at military installations within the NAVFAC Washington AOR, including Washington, DC, Maryland, Virginia, and other NAVFAC Atlantic locations. Projects will primarily involve design and engineering services for new construction, major renovations, and alterations with estimated construction values ranging from $5 million to $100 million, with the potential for larger, technically complex projects. Industrial services include, but are not limited to, multi-disciplinary A/E design and engineering services for single/multi-story facilities, high-bay (including hangars), masonry, concrete, steel, wood and pre-engineered types of facilities; research development test & evaluation (RDT&E) and manufacturing facilities; laboratory facilities; major civil projects; Anti-Terrorism/Force Protection analysis & design; MILCON construction design and MILCON Team Planning and Programming; and comprehensive planning projects. The type of services expected to be performed under this contract are listed below. The successful firm will show demonstrated experience in the following areas: Design of single or multi-story, high bay, masonry, concrete, steel, wood and pre-engineered types of structures and facilities. Design of industrial, research, and medical facilities ssuch as: water and sewer plants, steam and chilled water production plants, power generation plants, combined heat and power plants, hangars, airfield runways, taxiways and aprons, magazines, waterfront facilities, specialized training facilities, production and maintenance facilities, site improvements, research development test & evaluation (RDT&E) facilities, fire and rescue facilities, communication facilities, training and instructional facilities, wet laboratories, electronic laboratories, bio-safety laboratories, ISO 14644 clean rooms, and anechoic chambers. Wide range of facility designs in explosives safety support for RDT&E and manufacturing processes involving energetics and industrial chemicals. Such processes may range from laboratory-scale research and development to full-scale production, testing, storage, transport, and decontamination/disposal. The scope includes working within the constraints of explosives safety quantity-distance (ESQD) arcs and conforming to the requirements of NAVSEA OP-5 (Ammunition and Explosives Ashore, Safety Regulations for Handling, Storing, Production, Renovation, and Shipping), the National Environmental Policy Act (NEPA) and all associated federal, state, and local requirements; including the MCO 8020.10, Marine Corps Explosives Safety Management Program. Preparation and review of Preliminary and Final Explosives Site Safety Approvals in accordance with NAVFAC Regional Planning Instruction 11010.45 and NAVSEA OP-5, and demonstrated experience in the development of construction document packages for approval by the Naval Ordnance Safety and Security Activity (NOSSA), Marine Corps System Command (MARCORSYSCOM), and the Department of Defense Explosives Safety Board (DDESB). The work may also include miscellaneous explosives safety services. Depending upon the projects, consultations with regulatory agencies, such as the U.S. Fish and Wildlife Service (USFWS), state historic preservation offices (SHPO), and state environmental agencies will be required. Anti-Terrorism/Force Protection (ATFP) considerations including Unified Facility Criteria UFC DoD Minimum Antiterrorism Standards for Buildings (most recent version). Experience with renovated buildings incorporating progressive collapse design, secure facilities, progressive collapse design. Secure facilities with open storage secret spaces, sensitive compartmented information facilities (SCIFs), high altitude electromagnetic pulse (HEMP) shielding, Intrusion Detection Systems (IDS), and related features in accordance with NAVY/DoD related criteria Facility projects that incorporate photovoltaic systems, solar hot water heating, geothermal systems, and other new non-fossil fuel technologies. Preparation of miscellaneous studies; Requests for Proposals (RFPs) for Design-Build projects; and design and documentation for Design-Bid-Build projects. Preparation of MILCON DD Form 1391 Documentation, specifically Budget Final 1391 (including all requirements of the Region/FEC 1391) in accordance with the MILCON Team Planning and Programming Process (MTP3). Preparation of DASN notification packages for repair projects greater than $7.5 million, as well as miscellaneous planning services. title: Meteorological Weather Stations and Maintenance Support
description: Meteorological Weather Stations and Maintenance Support 1. Submittal Information: � Issue Date: August 10, 2026 � Response Date: August 24, 2026 � Submit Responses To: chora.snyder@dot.gov 2. Introduction: This is NOT a solicitation for proposals, proposal abstracts, or request for quotations. The Great Lakes St. Lawrence Seaway Development Corporation (GLS) is conducting market research to identify potential sources for an anticipated contract for the procurement, delivery, installation, IT configuration, and ongoing technical support of two (2) meteorological weather stations. The purpose of this notice is to obtain information, for planning purposes, regarding the availability and capability of qualified sources. The purpose of this notice is to obtain the following information: 1. Determine what sources exist that are capable of satisfying the Government�s requirement, 2. Determine the capability of potential contractors, 3. Determine the size and status of potential sources under NAICS 334519 � Other Measuring and Controlling Device Manufacturing, and 4. Determine the level of competition. 3. Requirement Description: The GLS is a wholly owned U.S. Government Corporation within the U.S. Department of Transportation which owns and operates that portion of the St. Lawrence Seaway in U.S. territorial waters between Lake Ontario and Montreal, Canada, including two navigation locks: Eisenhower and Snell Locks. The Corporation�s mission is to facilitate the safe and efficient passage of commercial vessels through the Seaway. GLS plans to issue a solicitation to standardize meteorological tracking equipment to ensure safe maritime transit and accurate scientific monitoring within its regional navigational channels. The contractor shall deliver, install, and assist in the configuration of two (2) Weather Stations, and provide ongoing technical support and maintenance via a dedicated service contract (1 Base Year + up to 4 Option Years) to maximize system operational uptime. GLS expects to evaluate prospective firms based on: 1. Specialized Hardware Experience: Capability to supply commercial-grade weather stations equipped with ultrasonic wind sensors, present weather detectors (MOR 10m to 20km, classifying seven precipitation types), battery management systems, and high-durability stainless steel enclosures rated for harsh sub-zero/high salinity environments. 2. IT & Telemetry Configuration Competence: Specialized experience bridging internal serial interfaces (RS-232/RS-485) to Ethernet architecture, streaming raw TCP/IP socket payloads (configurable cadence, e.g., 5 seconds), and customizing fixed-width or delimited payload schemas with user-defined prefixes and record terminators (CR, LF, CRLF). 3. Field Deployment & Installation Capabilities: Experience in physical deployment, structural securing, electrical routing, and network connectivity validation. 4. Maintenance & Support Capabilities: Capacity to provide multi-year remote technical guidance, software/firmware updates, and troubleshooting services. 4. Response: Interested firms shall submit the following: 1. Company Details: Name of Company; Company Address; Point of Contact (Name, Phone Number, and Email); Unique Entity Identifier (UEI); CAGE Code; and Socio-Economic Size Status under NAICS Code 334519 (Large/Small Business/HUBZone/8(a)/Woman-Owned Small Business/Service-Disabled Veteran-Owned Small Business/etc.). 2. Capability Statement: Provide a capability statement that lists up to three (3) projects similar in scope (hardware supply, sensor integration, network telemetry configuration, and maintenance), completed within the last 3 years. These projects may include services for commercial or federal entities. Brief descriptions of the relevant projects shall be provided along with contact references for each. (Not to exceed 3 pages). 3. Submission Method: Respond via email to chora.snyder@dot.gov. The email subject line must contain: Meteorological Weather Stations and Maintenance Support � Sources Sought 6923G526SS0006. Verbal questions will not be accepted and GLS will respond to written questions at its discretion. All communications must be sent via email to chora.snyder@dot.gov. Respondents to this notice should not anticipate feedback regarding their submission other than acknowledgement of receipt. GLS reserves the right to review late submissions but makes no guarantee that they will be reviewed. Results of this Notice will not be provided.

description: Document Type: Combined Synopsis/Solicitation Solicitation Number: 15BCTS26Q00000003 Posted Date: August 3, 2026 Original Response Date: August 24, 2026 Current Response Date: August 24, 2026 Product or Service Code: G004 Set Aside: Total Small Business Concerns NAICS Code: 621420 Contracting Office Address Federal Bureau of Prisons Community Treatment Services Contracting 320 First Street NW, 2nd Floor Washington, DC 20534 318-561-5304 (phone) j15walker@bop.gov (email) Description This is a combined synopsis/solicitation for commercial products or services prepared in accordance with Federal Acquisition Regulation (FAR) Part 12. This announcement constitutes the only solicitation. Quotes are being requested, and a separate written solicitation will not be issued. Solicitation number 15BCTS26Q00000003 is issued as a request for quotation (RFQ). The Federal Bureau of Prisons, CTS Contracting Office, is seeking quotes from sources that have the ability to provide community-based outpatient for a national peer support service in the community to augment traditional mental health and substance use disorder treatment for inmates currently participating in Community Treatment Services and to provide reentry peer support for all inmates in community placement. The service will be delivered via mobile application utilizing tele-support or video-support mechanisms by certified peer support specialists to inmates in community placement on cellular phones, laptops, and tablets. Community Reentry Peer Support shall be made available to the inmate population 365 days a year, seven days per week, from 7:00 am to 10:00 pm, local time of the location where peer support services are being provided. Outside of these hours, inmates shall be given contact information for other support options, such as crisis lines, hotlines, or lifelines, for urgent crisis situations. Title: Production of ChAdOx-1 and MVA expressing mouse gp70 Document type: Combined Synopsis/Intent to Sole Source Solicitation Number: RFQ# 75N98026Q00996 Proposed Post Date: 08/12/2026 Proposed Response Date: 08/19/2026 NAICS Code: 541714 Small Business Size Standard: 1,000 Contracting Office Address: Department of Health and Human Services, National Institutes of Health, 6701 Rockledge Drive, Bethesda, MD 20817 USA. Description: The National Cancer Center�s (NCI) Laboratory of Integrative Cancer Immunology Branch / The Immune Regulation and Vaccine Development Section intends to award a sole-source purchase order using the procedures at FAR 13.106-1(b)(1), as it has been deemed that only one source is available to meet this specific requirement to provide service of producing chimpanzee adenovirus (ChAdOx-1) vectors and MVA viral vector expressing mouse gp70. This purchase order is intended to be awarded to Viral Vector Core at the Pandemic Institute, University of Oxford, Pandemic Science Institute - University of Oxford Old Road Campus Research Building (ORCRB), Oxford, OX3 7DQ, Oxford, OX3 7DQ. The requirements document in the form of a Statement of Work is attached to this notice. The North American Industry Classification System code is 541714 �Research and Development in Biotechnology (except Nanobiotechnology)� and the business size standard is 1,000 employees. In the development of a vaccine for glioblastoma, a high-grade brain tumor, there has been use of a combination of ChAdOx and MVA in syngeneic orthotopic mouse glioblastoma models. This has demonstrated this combination significantly prolongs the survival of tumor-bearing animals by inducing a robust population of tumor-specific CD8 T cells in the brain. The selection of this set of viral vectors, particularly the chimpanzee adenovirus ChAdOx-1, is to overcome the issue of pre-existing immunity to human adenoviruses. As the goal of this project is to evaluate the vaccine�s efficacy in protecting against breast cancer brain metastasis, it is essential to use the same viral vector platform, the vendor currently providing chimpanzee adenovirus-based vectors. The Contractor shall provide/perform the following, unless otherwise noted: TECHNICAL REQUIREMENTS: Design and construction of a codon-optimized gene expression cassette encoding mouse gp70 and the mouse class II major histocompatibility complex invariant chain (Ii) for expression in mouse cells. Production of a ChAdOx-1 viral vector encoding the gene construct. Production of an MVA viral vector encoding the same gene construct. Viral Vector Core at the Pandemic Institute, University of Oxford is the only known vendor currently provide chimpanzee adenovirus-based vectors as this is the proprietary technology owned by the Viral Vector Core of the University of Oxford. (2) Critical and major welds may be subjected to further non destructive testing (such as dye penetrant inspection)as prescribed by the buying activity. (3) Proper documentation shall be available for review by Government personnel. 3.5 WORK INSTRUCTIONS. Work instructions shall be posted at theoperator's work station giving procedures to control the welding process, i.e., filler material, weld size, electrical and gas characteristics, including flow rate. 3.6 MATERIALS AND MATERIALS CONTROL. The quality program shall assure that the materials used in fabrication or processing, i.e., base metals and weld filler material, be inspected and conform to the applicable physical, chemical and other technical requirements (supplier's certification is sufficient). 3.7 CONTROLS. Weld filler materials shall be clearly identified and segregated from each other both when in storage and at the work station. Work station environment shall be controlled to prevent conditions adverse to proper gas shielding. 3.8 CLEANING. Parts to be welded shall be cleaned to remove surface soils such as oils, waxes, grease, inks, etc. except that uninhibited alkaline solutions such as sodium hydroxide shall NOT be used. 3.9 DEOXIDIZING. The cleaned parts shall be chemically deoxidized NO MORE THAN 10 DAYS PRIOR TO WELDING to remove thick surface oxide films. (If the material or work is exposed to an outdoor environment, this time limit shall be reduced to a maximum of 3 days, to account for atmospheric effects.) Mechanical cleaning methods shall be applied just prior to the actual start of welding, to remove any reoxidation or residual thin oxide films. 3.9.1 CHEMICAL TREATMENT. An acid deoxidizing treatment shall be applied by either immersion or brushing/wiping. Deoxidizers acceptable for use shall include nitric acid, sulfuric chromic, phosphoric chromic, or equivalent solutions. Sodium hydroxide solutions shall not be used. Care shall be taken to assure 100% solution coverage of the area to be welded. To allow an adequately sized deoxidized area for good welding, the solution shall be applied to an area extending at least 2 inches from the weld site, or ending at any closer adjacent edge. 3.9.2 MECHANICAL MEANS. Immediately prior to welding, mechanical cleaning methods shall be applied to the weld areas previously chemically treated to assure removal of residual or reformed oxides, if any. Acceptable methods of mechanical cleaning include stainless steel wire brushing, scraping, filing, or sanding. However, abrasives containing iron and its oxides, steel wool and wire, and copper alloy based wire, which may become embedded with galvanically active metals and accelerate corrosion of aluminum alloys shall NOT be used. Mechanical methods shall be vigorous enough to adequately remove any residual oxide films, but gentle

The solicitation document and incorporated provisions and clauses are those in effect through Federal Acquisition Circular (FAC) 2026-03. Requirement Description: The USDA Forest Service, Region 6 (Pacific Northwest Region), requires professional laboratory services to perform Per- and Polyfluoroalkyl Substances (PFAS) drinking water analysis for seventy-five (75) non-public or public transient drinking water systems. Testing is mandated by internal USFS policy to protect personnel and the public. The selected laboratory must provide all necessary sample containers, coolers, cold packs, written technical sampling instructions, and pre-paid return shipping labels to various remote Forest Service Point of Contact (POC) locations. No sample gathering labor is required from the contractor. Laboratory Certifications & Technical Methods: To be considered for award, the laboratory performing the tests MUST possess a current certification for PFAS analysis from either the State of Oregon or the State of Washington. The laboratory must be certified to run specific US EPA approved analytical methods: EPA Method 533, 537.1, or 537. Proof of current certification must be submitted with the quotation package. Schedule of Items (CLIN Breakdown): CLIN 0001: Shipping and Handling - Mail sample bottles, QA/QC materials (trip blanks), shipping materials, and return labels to water system POCs. Quantity: 75 EA. (Unit price must include analysis costs for up to 19 trip blanks, representing 25% of systems). CLIN 0002: Analyze Drinking Water Samples - Receive, process, and perform PFAS laboratory analysis. Quantity: 75 EA. CLIN 0003: Compiled Results - Consolidate all laboratory report findings into a single Excel table/spreadsheet format. Quantity: 1 Lump Sum. Period of Performance & Location: All collection supplies must be mailed out within 30 days of contract award. All laboratory testing must be completed and standard reports emailed by November 30, 2026. Final compiled Excel results must be submitted by December 31, 2026. Work will be performed at the laboratory�s home facility; no travel is required Evaluation and Basis for Award: Award will be made to a single responsive and responsible offeror representing the most advantageous solution to the Government. Quotes will be evaluated in accordance with FAR Part 12.203 based on the following criteria: Technical Capability (Proof of valid OR/WA certification and required EPA methods) Past Performance (Evaluated as Acceptable, Neutral, or Unacceptable) Price (Evaluated for fairness and reasonableness) Submission Instructions: Vendors must have an Active Registration in SAM.gov at the time of submission. Quotation packages must include: Completed SF-1449 (Blocks 17a, 30a, 30b, and 30c, including Telephone, Email, and Unique Entity ID). Pricing completed for all individual line items within the Schedule of Items. Relevant Experience / Past Performance references. Physical or electronic proof of valid Oregon or Washington PFAS analytical laboratory certification. All signed and dated offers must be submitted via email to Mindy Hickman at mindy.hickman@usda.gov no later than August 24, 2026, at 11:00 AM PDT. Late or incomplete packages will be excluded from consideration.

description: Title: Production of ChAdOx-1 and MVA expressing mouse gp70 Document type: Combined Synopsis/Intent to Sole Source Solicitation Number: RFQ# 75N98026Q00996 Proposed Post Date: 08/12/2026 Proposed Response Date: 08/19/2026 NAICS Code: 541714 Small Business Size Standard: 1,000 Contracting Office Address: Department of Health and Human Services, National Institutes of Health, 6701 Rockledge Drive, Bethesda, MD 20817 USA. Description: The National Cancer Center�s (NCI) Laboratory of Integrative Cancer Immunology Branch / The Immune Regulation and Vaccine Development Section intends to award a sole-source purchase order using the procedures at FAR 13.106-1(b)(1), as it has been deemed that only one source is available to meet this specific requirement to provide service of producing chimpanzee adenovirus (ChAdOx-1) vectors and MVA viral vector expressing mouse gp70. This purchase order is intended to be awarded to Viral Vector Core at the Pandemic Institute, University of Oxford, Pandemic Science Institute - University of Oxford Old Road Campus Research Building (ORCRB), Oxford, OX3 7DQ, Oxford, OX3 7DQ. The requirements document in the form of a Statement of Work is attached to this notice. The acquisition will be processed in accordance with Sole Source Selection procedures as stated in FAR Part 6.302-1 and 41 U.S.C. 3304(a)(1and is exempt from the requirements of FAR Part 6. The North American Industry Classification System code is 541714 �Research and Development in Biotechnology (except Nanobiotechnology)� and the business size standard is 1,000 employees. In the development of a vaccine for glioblastoma, a high-grade brain tumor, there has been use of a combination of ChAdOx and MVA in syngeneic orthotopic mouse glioblastoma models. This has demonstrated this combination significantly prolongs the survival of tumor-bearing animals by inducing a robust population of tumor-specific CD8 T cells in the brain. The selection of this set of viral vectors, particularly the chimpanzee adenovirus ChAdOx-1, is to overcome the issue of pre-existing immunity to human adenoviruses. As the goal of this project is to evaluate the vaccine�s efficacy in protecting against breast cancer brain metastasis, it is essential to use the same viral vector platform, the vendor currently providing chimpanzee adenovirus-based vectors. The Contractor shall provide/perform the following, unless otherwise noted: TECHNICAL REQUIREMENTS: Design and construction of a codon-optimized gene expression cassette encoding mouse gp70 and the mouse class II major histocompatibility complex invariant chain (Ii) for expression in mouse cells. Production of a ChAdOx-1 viral vector encoding the gene construct. Production of an MVA viral vector encoding the same gene construct. Viral Vector Core at the Pandemic Institute, University of Oxford is the only known vendor currently provide chimpanzee adenovirus-based vectors as this is the proprietary technology owned by the Viral Vector Core of the University of Oxford. REPORTING REQUIREMENTS AND DELIVERABLES: The period of performance shall be 6 months from the date of award. All deliverables included in the Statement of Work will be submitted to: the Contracting Officer�s Representative, Alan Peigh, and Sharon Bargo, Ph.D. The Contractor that receives the award will be provided with the complete mailing address and points of contact. Anti-Terrorism/Force Protection (ATFP) considerations including Unified Facility Criteria UFC DoD Minimum Antiterrorism Standards for Buildings (most recent version). Preparation of DASN notification packages for repair projects greater than $7.5 million, as well as miscellaneous planning services. Design services including programming, design and engineering concepts, contract documents, construction cost estimates, value engineering studies, cost and schedule risk analysis (CSRA), quality control and quality assurance activities, surveys, shop drawing reviews, construction consultation and inspection. Preparation of construction record drawings, DD Forms 1354, and eOMSI facility data workbooks. Use of NAVFAC eCMS and/or Kahua for submittal processing. Interior design services including design, specification, procurement, installation coordination, and construction management services for both Comprehensive Interior Design (CID), which includes Structural Interior Design (SID) and Furniture, Fixtures & Equipment (FF&E). description: Notice Type: Sources Sought Notice ID: N4008026RAEIDIQINDUSTRIAL Date: Tuesday, July 21, 2026 Response Date: Monday, August 24, 2026, 2:00 PM EST NAICS: 541330-Engineering Services This is a Sources Sought Notice. This notice does not constitute a request for proposal, request for quote, or invitation for bid. The intent of this notice is to identify potential offerors for market research purposes and determine whether to set aside this requirement for small business concerns, including firms certified by the U.S. Small Business Administration (SBA) as 8(a), HUBZone, Service-Disabled Veteran-Owned Small Business (SDVOSB), Women-Owned Small Business (WOSB), or Economically Disadvantaged Women-Owned Small Business (EDWOSB), with the qualifications, experience, personnel, and capability to perform multidisciplinary architect-engineering (A/E) services in support of projects at military installations within the Naval Facilities Engineering Systems Command (NAVFAC) Washington Area of Responsibility (AOR), including Washington, DC, Maryland, and Virginia (DMV). TELEPHONIC SUBMISSIONS AND QUESTIONS WILL NOT BE ACCEPTED OR ACKNOWLEDGED AS THIS IS A SOURCES SOUGHT NOTICE ONLY. In accordance with FAR 15.201(e), responses to this notice are not offers and cannot be accepted by the Government to form a binding contract. The Government will not pay or reimburse respondents for any costs, administrative expenses, or effort associated with preparing or submitting information in response to this announcement or any subsequent follow-up requests. All costs associated with responding will be solely at the interested party's expense. No basis for a claim against the Government shall arise from responding to this Sources Sought Notice. NAVFAC Washington anticipates awarding two stand-alone Indefinite Delivery/Indefinite Quantity (IDIQ) Architect-Engineering (A/E) contracts: the "Blue" NAVFAC Washington Regional A/E IDIQ and the "Gold" NAVFAC Washington Regional A/E IDIQ. The anticipated maximum value of each contract is $249,000,000. Each contract is expected to include a two-year base period, a three-year option period, and a six-month extension option. NAVFAC Washington seeks qualified firms with relevant experience, personnel, and capabilities to provide multidisciplinary A/E services for projects at military installations within the NAVFAC Washington AOR, including Washington, DC, Maryland, Virginia, and other NAVFAC Atlantic locations. Projects will primarily involve design and engineering services for new construction, major renovations, and alterations with estimated construction values ranging from $5 million to $100 million, with the potential for larger, technically complex projects. Industrial services include, but are not limited to, multi-disciplinary A/E design and engineering services for single/multi-story facilities, high-bay (including hangars), masonry, concrete, steel, wood and pre-engineered types of facilities; research development test & evaluation (RDT&E) and manufacturing facilities; laboratory facilities; major civil projects; Anti-Terrorism/Force Protection analysis & design; MILCON construction design and MILCON Team Planning and Programming; and comprehensive planning projects. The type of services expected to be performed under this contract are listed below. The successful firm will show demonstrated experience in the following areas: Design of single or multi-story, high bay, masonry, concrete, steel, wood and pre-engineered types of structures and facilities. Design of industrial, research, and medical facilities ssuch as: water and sewer plants, steam and chilled water production plants, power generation plants, combined heat and power plants, hangars, airfield runways, taxiways and aprons, magazines, waterfront facilities, specialized training facilities, production and maintenance facilities, site improvements, research development test & evaluation (RDT&E) facilities, fire and rescue facilities, communication facilities, training and instructional facilities, wet laboratories, electronic laboratories, bio-safety laboratories, ISO 14644 clean rooms, and anechoic chambers. Wide range of facility designs in explosives safety support for RDT&E and manufacturing processes involving energetics and industrial chemicals. Such processes may range from laboratory-scale research and development to full-scale production, testing, storage, transport, and decontamination/disposal. The scope includes working within the constraints of explosives safety quantity-distance (ESQD) arcs and conforming to the requirements of NAVSEA OP-5 (Ammunition and Explosives Ashore, Safety Regulations for Handling, Storing, Production, Renovation, and Shipping), the National Environmental Policy Act (NEPA) and all associated federal, state, and local requirements; including the MCO 8020.10, Marine Corps Explosives Safety Management Program. Preparation and review of Preliminary and Final Explosives Site Safety Approvals in accordance with NAVFAC Regional Planning Instruction 11010.45 and NAVSEA OP-5, and demonstrated experience in the development of construction document packages for approval by the Naval Ordnance Safety and Security Activity (NOSSA), Marine Corps System Command (MARCORSYSCOM), and the Department of Defense Explosives Safety Board (DDESB). The work may also include miscellaneous explosives safety services. Depending upon the projects, consultations with regulatory agencies, such as the U.S. Fish and Wildlife Service (USFWS), state historic preservation offices (SHPO), and state environmental agencies will be required. Anti-Terrorism/Force Protection (ATFP) considerations including Unified Facility Criteria UFC DoD Minimum Antiterrorism Standards for Buildings (most recent version). Experience with renovated buildings incorporating progressive collapse design, secure facilities, progressive collapse design. Secure facilities with open storage secret spaces, sensitive compartmented information facilities (SCIFs), high altitude electromagnetic pulse (HEMP) shielding, Intrusion Detection Systems (IDS), and related features in accordance with NAVY/DoD related criteria Facility projects that incorporate photovoltaic systems, solar hot water heating, geothermal systems, and other new non-fossil fuel technologies. Preparation of miscellaneous studies; Requests for Proposals (RFPs) for Design-Build projects; and design and documentation for Design-Bid-Build projects. Preparation of MILCON DD Form 1391 Documentation, specifically Budget Final 1391 (including all requirements of the Region/FEC 1391) in accordance with the MILCON Team Planning and Programming Process (MTP3). Preparation of DASN notification packages for repair projects greater than $7.5 million, as well as miscellaneous planning services. Design services including programming, design and engineering concepts, contract documents, construction cost estimates, value engineering studies, cost and schedule risk analysis (CSRA), quality control and quality assurance activities, surveys, shop drawing reviews, construction consultation and inspection. Preparation of construction record drawings, DD Forms 1354, and eOMSI facility data workbooks. Use of NAVFAC eCMS and/or Kahua for submittal processing. Preparation of comprehensive stormwater management and Low Impact Development (LID) plans that are required for the State of Maryland, the District of Columbia, and the Commonwealth of Virginia or other comprehensive stormwater management plans for localities as may be required for other NAVFAC Atlantic sites. Interior design services including design, specification, procurement, installation coordination, and construction management services for both Comprehensive Interior Design (CID), which includes Structural Interior Design (SID) and Furniture, Fixtures & Equipment (FF&E). title: 15BCTS26Q00000003 - National Peer Support
description: Document Type: Combined Synopsis/Solicitation Solicitation Number: 15BCTS26Q00000003 Posted Date: August 3, 2026 Original Response Date: August 24, 2026 Current Response Date: August 24, 2026 Product or Service Code: G004 Set Aside: Total Small Business Concerns NAICS Code: 621420 Contracting Office Address Federal Bureau of Prisons Community Treatment Services Contracting 320 First Street NW, 2nd Floor Washington, DC 20534 318-561-5304 (phone) j15walker@bop.gov (email) Description This is a combined synopsis/solicitation for commercial products or services prepared in accordance with Federal Acquisition Regulation (FAR) Part 12. This announcement constitutes the only solicitation. Quotes are being requested, and a separate written solicitation will not be issued. Solicitation number 15BCTS26Q00000003 is issued as a request for quotation (RFQ). The Federal Bureau of Prisons, CTS Contracting Office, is seeking quotes from sources that have the ability to provide community-based outpatient for a national peer support service in the community to augment traditional mental health and substance use disorder treatment for inmates currently participating in Community Treatment Services and to provide reentry peer support for all inmates in community placement. The service will be delivered via mobile application utilizing tele-support or video-support mechanisms by certified peer support specialists to inmates in community placement on cellular phones, laptops, and tablets. Community Reentry Peer Support shall be made available to the inmate population 365 days a year, seven days per week, from 7:00 am to 10:00 pm, local time of the location where peer support services are being provided. Outside of these hours, inmates shall be given contact information for other support options, such as crisis lines, hotlines, or lifelines, for urgent crisis situations. The peer support service will provide proactive support to inmates in community placement; identify risk factors for relapse and recidivism and offer direct support to navigate these challenges; improve mental health outcomes; and assist inmates in becoming law-abiding citizens, which aligns with the FBOP�s mission to provide self-improvement opportunities. Simplified acquisition procedures are being used and anticipated award date is September 10, 2026. This acquisition is set aside for small business concerns. This solicitation incorporates provisions and clauses by reference. The full text of provisions and clauses may be accessed electronically at www.acquisition.gov. The associated North American Industrial Classification System (NAICS) code for this procurement is 621420, with a small business size standard of $19,000,000. The product or service code is G004. The government will award an indefinite-delivery contract resulting from this combined synopsis/solicitation to the responsible offeror whose offer, conforming to the synopsis/solicitation, will be most advantageous to the government (as determined by the solicitation evaluation criteria). Performance Period (09/10/2026 - 12/31/2026): Estimated Number of Community Reentry Peer Support Services (CRPSS) Units 1030 CRPSS-Basic � 10 Units Guaranteed Minimum; 1015 Units Estimated Maximum 1040 CRPSS-Standard � 5 Units Guaranteed Minimum; 600 Units Estimated Maximum 1050 CRPSS-Enhanced � 3 Units Guaranteed Minimum; 250 Units Estimated Maximum Services The contractor shall be capable of providing outpatient virtual peer support services for basic, standard, and enhanced treatment services to offenders confined in community-based programs nationwide. These services shall be in accordance with the Federal Bureau of Prisons (BOP) Community Treatment Services (CTS) Statement of Work (SOW) Virtual CRPSS, dated May 2026. The period of performance is estimated to begin on September 10, 2026 and no option to extend, with services ending on December 31, 2026. Place of Performance This is a virtual reentry peer support service and does not have a location of service designated. All references to Residential Re-Entry Center (RRC) and Community Correctional Center (CCC) shall be treated equally for the purpose of this contract. Deliveries In accordance with Federal Acquisition Regulation (FAR) 16.505, and the clause located in FAR 52.216-18, Ordering, states that any supplies or services to be furnished under this contract shall be ordered by issuance of task orders by a warranted Contracting Officer in the CTS Contracting Office. Freedom of Information Act The Freedom of Information Act (FOIA) and its amendments have resulted in an increasing number of requests to Federal Agencies for copies of Technical/Management and Business Proposals from other than Government sources. The offeror should identify information in its Technical/Management and Business Proposals the offeror believes should be withheld from these sources, on the basis the proposals consist of "trade secrets and commercial or financial information obtained from a person and privileged or confidential" (exemption (b) (4) of the FOIA). This identification will assist in the decision by a responsible federal official to disclose or withhold the requested information. If an offeror considers elements of its proposal to be exempt under FOIA, ensure the following notice is annotated on the title page of the quote: Elements of this document, as identified on individual pages, are considered by the submitter to be privileged or confidential trade secrets or commercial or financial information not subject to mandatory disclosure under the Freedom of Information Act. Material considered privileged or confidential on this basis is contained on pages ____. The offeror must annotate each individual item it considers privileged or confidential under the FOIA exemption with the following notice: The data or information is considered confidential or privileged, and not subject to mandatory disclosure under the FOIA. All information in an offeror's quote not designated may be subject to automatic public disclosure if it is requested under the FOIA. It must be emphasized that under the FOIA no information is automatically exempt from public disclosure. However, no disclosures will be made without careful evaluation, giving due regard to the need for safeguarding material considered privileged or confidential by the offeror. It is Department of Justice policy to withhold whenever possible material that is genuinely privileged or confidential. Billing Information The Government will make payment on a monthly basis via Electronic Fund Transfer. Invoices with the contract number should be submitted electronically to BOP-RSD-CRBCTS-BILL-DC-S@bop.gov. Contractors that are classified as a small business are required to indicate their small business size status on each invoice submitted for payment. Award Without Discussions Award will be made to the quoter whose quotation offers the best value to the government, considering technical capability and lowest price technically available. Quoters are advised an award may be made without discussions. The Contracting Officer cannot overemphasize the necessity for the initial quotation of a quoter to provide the Government with sufficient information identifying the quoter's best terms from a cost or price and technical standpoint. By using the documentation submitted with each quotation, an initial review will also be conducted to determine whether it meets the minimum requirements contained in the Decisional Rule Criteria below. title: BAFS Flight Line Debris and Restoration
description: The project priority is removal of all vehicles, tires, debris, scrap metal, large rocks, 7 acres of plants and vegetation, asphalt piles, DRMO assets, from within the project area. This project will support Bellows Air Force Station (BAFS) complete invasive species management requirements from the 2025 BAFS Integrated Natural Resource Management Plan (INRMP). The project priority is removal and mulching of all vegetation including invasive ironwood trees (Casuarina equisetifolia) and the resulting wood product from within the project area. This route is also used in emergency scenarios by first responders to transport patients in critical condition. In the current state, it is unsafe to transport patients. These vegetation piles, asphalt piles, and DRMO assets all have Environmental CRB impacts and hazards. The current area is a fire hazard and needs to be eradicated appropriately through proper disposal channels. *AMENDMENT 0003* Made edits to details highlighted in yellow within Attachment 1 PWS BAFS Flightline Amendment 0003. title: Notice of Intent (NOI) to Sole Source and Request for Information (RFI)
description: Notice of Intent (NOI) to Sole Source AND Request for Information (RFI) Notice of Intent (NOI) to sole source electrical utility services to Consumer Energy as part of the Tar Lake Superfund environmental remediation services contract. The Tar Lake Superfund project is located in Mancelona Township, Michigan. Description: The U.S. Army Corps of Engineers (USACE), Detroit District, anticipates publicizing a solicitation for an environmental remediation services contract for the Tar Lake Superfund project located in Mancelona Township, MI. As part of this procurement, USACE Detroit District intends to specify a portion of the acquisition on a sole source basis under the authority of Revolutionary FAR Overhaul 6.103-1 One Responsible Source to Consumers Energy for all necessary Electrical Service connections and subsequent electrical supply service. The required sole source elements consist of connecting existing electrical service infrastructure owned by Consumers Energy to the new biosparge building that the Contractor receiving the forthcoming contract will erect and then the subsequent supply of electrical services to that building. Consumers Energy is the sole electrical services provider in the project area. The prime contractor must coordinate work to complete the connection to be performed by Consumers Energy or their subcontractor and the electrical supply provision must be performed by Consumers Energy. No other source can satisfy the government�s requirement. Disclaimer This NOI is being issued to provide notification of the Government�s intent to sole source the electric utility portion of the requirement and obtain industry feedback through the RFI process. This is not a request for a competitive proposal. This is not a solicitation, and the information contained herein is subject to change or be eliminated from the requirement. Only firms capable of providing a compatible a compatible equivalent product are requested to respond by email. Oral communications are not acceptable in response to this notice. Responses Interested parties able to source and procure a directly compatible equivalent product may identify their interest and capability in writing to the identified points of contact below, no later than August 24, 2026, at 2:00pm (Eastern). Please include the following in your response: 1. Name of Firm 2. UEI or Cage Code 3. Point of Contract, Phone Number, and Email Address 4. Supporting documentation to illustrate the directly compatible equivalent product(s). Submit any information for consideration by the Government via email to the Contract Specialist and Contracting Officer listed below using the Subject Line: NOI for Tar Lake Superfund -Consumers Energy Sole Source. Reminder Responses shall be evaluated solely for the purpose of determining whether or not to conduct this portion of the procurement on a competitive basis. A determination by the Government, based upon responses received from this notice, is solely at the discretion of the Government.

title: Chena River Lakes Flood Control Project - Floor Drain Disposal
description: The Chena River Lakes Flood Control Project (Chena Project) has one shop floor holding tank that is not connected to a leach field and must be pumped to be emptied. The holding tank water will either be pumped directly from the shop floor holding tank or from plastic totes situated in the shop next to the drain in a heated space. The holding tank contents will be pumped, transported, and disposed under this contract. The Chena Project is located 3800 Laurance Road, North Pole, Alaska, approximately 18 miles east of Fairbanks, Alaska. The Contractor shall furnish all labor, supervision, equipment, tools, parts and materials, as necessary, for the pumping and disposal of shop tank contents. Test results for the holding tank contents are shown in the Holding Tank Test Sample Analysis. The Contractor is solely responsible for following any AKDEC and Federal regulations as they pertain to proper disposal of the holding tank contents. The contractor shall possess all required licenses and permits for transporting the holding tank contents. See RFQ for more details.
